FINITE HETERODYNE ADMISSION BEFORE USEFUL QUANTUM INPUT
Astra P2 / Phase 8. Root construction. 1 November 2026.

Problem and result
==================
The repeated-use proof needs an exponential moment, not an initial mean alone.
Finite passive cooling cannot turn an arbitrary heavy-tailed input into a
uniform exponential-moment family. The earlier n<=100 precondition is therefore
replaced, in this OPTIONAL explicit startup route, by a real finite heterodyne
accept/abort instrument. The initial mean is used only for availability and a
once-only startup noise comparison. The accepted instrument earns the moment.

This occurs before useful quantum input is loaded or encoded. It is not a
measurement of a running logical qubit. All retained-state correlations created
during later operations remain allowed. The extra simultaneous two-quadrature
receiver is a real physical capability and is also available to competitors.
Neither arbitrary initially correlated useful data nor a free startup flag is
assumed. Raw heterodyne values are internal and retired after the accept bit.

1. The actual acceptance instrument
==================================
Passively cool with the same physical port, then observe it for a finite
window T. Uniformly integrate both heterodyne quadratures: f(t)=1/sqrt(T).
Use two16-bit ADCs on[-16,16]. Their step is1/2048 in normalized complex-amplitude
coordinates. Accept exactly when the integer squared radius is at most the
radius corresponding to R=4. Saturation at +/-16 produces an abort. The sum
of two squares and comparison fit a40-bit signed protected register.

This is a finite analog integrator followed by two finite ADCs and an integer
test; it does not require an optical quantum mode selector or photon counter.
The physical integrator response and detector covariance/efficiency are stated
model conditions. Their faults and actual decision latency are charged below.

Let delta_R=sqrt(2)/(4096), R_plus=4+delta_R, R_minus=4-delta_R.
Every actually accepted uncorrupted ADC record has true |beta|<=R_plus.
Conversely |beta|<=R_minus guarantees acceptance. A clipped integrated output
cannot be accepted because its integer magnitude already exceeds the radius.

# Independent audit: finite heterodyne startup admission

## Decision

The proposed startup is mathematically sound in its stated passive, linear, homogeneous thermal model. A real finite heterodyne acceptance disk can turn a mere initial mean bound into an exponential-moment bound on the accepted reference state. The acceptance effect supplies the tail; passive cooling alone does not.

The operator inequality holds for arbitrary initial oscillator–reference correlations and even for inputs with no exponential moment. The finite mean assumption is needed separately to lower-bound availability and to bound a once-only comparison with unwanted startup forces. For many initially correlated buses, the correct normalization uses a global success lower bound from unconditional marginals and a union bound. Multiplying conditional per-bus success probabilities would be unjustified.

I found one small missing step in the first root writeup: the final decision interval needs an exponential-moment propagation bound, rather than a statement about its mean. With the readout port closed, the proposed `.05/g` interval adds less than `6.741e-7` to the log-moment bound. Root has now incorporated this term. The startup perturbation estimate is a **half trace-distance** bound; full trace norm has the extra factor two. The tighter damped-mean comparison added subsequently is also sound; Section 9 audits it.

This audit concerns the construction in `phase8/root/FINITE_STARTUP_ADMISSION.txt`, its numerical implementation in `finite_heterodyne_admission.py`, and the parent’s correlated-array extension. No root file was changed during this audit.

## 1. Physical model and actual finite acceptance

Let `a` be the old oscillator and let `c` be an independent thermal mode of occupation `n_b`. A passive window with surviving intensity `r` has a dilation

\[
a_{\rm ret}=\sqrt r\,a+\sqrt{1-r}\,c,
\qquad
b=-\sqrt{1-r}\,a+\sqrt r\,c.
\]

The collective complementary output `b` includes all loss ports. A normalized measured temporal output mode has the form

\[
s=\sqrt\mu\,b+\sqrt{1-\mu}\,h,
\]

after absorbing an irrelevant phase into the mode definition. Here `h` is an independent thermal mode of the same occupation.
